DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilg.gov.ph DILG OPINION No. 92 s. 2022 15 September 2022 MS. FE CARRANZA-IGNACIO Secretary to the Sangguniang Bayan Municipality of Baras Province of Catanduanes Dear Ms. Carranza-Ignacio: This has reference to your letter dated 21 March 2022 seeking legal opinion from this Department on the following: I. Whether or not the DILG MC No. 2020-027 amended the power of the Municipality to implement ordinances in their respective territorial jurisdiction. 2. Whether or not the Municipal Ordinance No. 2-2021 of Baras is valid and may be implemented in national roads following the DILG MC No. 2020- 027. Per your representation, the Municipality of Baras passed Municipal Ordinance No. 2- 2021 entitled "AN ORDINANCE REGULATING THE USE OF STREETS, SIDEWALKS, ALLEYS AND BRIDGES AND THE USE OF BUSINESS SIGNAGES ALONG THE STREETS IN THE MUNICIPALITY OF BARAS, CATANDUANES" You also represented that the ordinance was submitted for review and confirmation of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan but the latter claims that the ordinance violates the mentioned Memorandum Circular since the ordinance should only apply to the municipal roads and not to the national roads. The Sangguniang Panlalawigan then ordered the Sangguniang Bayan of Baras to specify the scope of the municipal and barangay roads and that the ordinance should not include the provincial and national roads in the scope of implementation. Hence, the instant queries. As to the first guery, please be informed that this Department has no authority to amend the power of any municipality to implement ordinances, or the power to amend any ordinance enacted by the Sanggunian- Primarily, MC No 2020-027 enjoins the Local Govemment Units to enact or review existing ordinance/s that provide for the conduct of road clearing operations and conduct an inventory of roads within its jurisdiction. The said MC does not amend the power of "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

any municipality to implement their ordinances, but rather, it only directs all LGUs to clear roads of illegal obstructions, and pursuant to Section 17(b) of the LGC, it mandates all LGUs to manage and maintain roads within their jurisdiction as a basic service and facility. Thus, MC No 2020-027 cannot encroach the power of any municipality to implement ordinances, and it definitely cannot amend any ordinance enacted by the Sanggunian. As to the second query. please be apprised that this Department, in its previous legal opinions, has been consistent that inasmuch as the ordinance has undergone the procedural process for its enactment pursuant to the Local Govemment Code of 1991 (LGC), the same is considered valid unless declared otherwise by courts. Accordingly, this Department is bereft of authority to rule on the legality of the subject ordinance in question as this is within the jurisdiction of the regular courts. Thus, any issues concerning the validity of an ordinance shall be threshed out by the proper court. Notwithstanding, for purposes of academic discussion, this Department has already settled that duly approved ordinances are presumptively valid acts and thus, enjoy the presumption of regularity on the part of the public concemed.l Clearly, matters involving questions on the validity or constitutionality of a duly enacted ordinances may stand on its own and therefore remain valid until judicially declared as null and void.2 Similarly, DILG Opinion No.5, s. 2018, dated 25 January 2018, has long settled the distinction between the terms "effectivity" and "validity" of an ordinance as they are two different things. Effectivity is the time by which an ordinance is made effective and can already be implemented and given full force and effect. Effectivity is govemed by Section 59(a) of the Local Govemment Code of 1991 , thus: "Section 59. Effectivity of Ordinances or Resolutions. - (a) Unless otherwise stated in the ordinance or the resolution approving the local development plan and public investment program, the same shall take effect after ten (IO) days from the date a copy thereof is posted in a bulletin board at the entrance of the provincial capitol or city, municipal, or barangay hall, as the case may be, and in at least two (2) other conspicuous places in the local government unit concerned." Based on Section 59(a) of the LGC, an ordinance of a local government unit becomes effective as of the framers of such ordinance would like it to be effective and in the absence of such effectivity clause, the same shall take effect after ten (10) days from the date a copy thereof is posted in a bulletin board at the entrance of the municipal hall in at least two (2) other conspicuous places in the local govemment unit concerned. 1 DILG opinion NO. 29 s. 2019, dated 24 June 2019 Citing DILG Opinion NO. 24, s. 2011 2 Ibid Page 2 of 4

Validity on the other hand, refers to the substantive requirement of an ordinance, whether the same is consistent with the Constitution and laws. The pertinent provision of the LGC provides that: Section 56. Review of Component City and Municipal Ordinances or Resolutions by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan. (a) Within three (3) days after approval, the secretary to the sanggunian panlungsod or sangguniang bayan shall forward to the sangguniang panlalawigan for review, copies of approved ordinances and the resolutions approving the local development plans and public investment programs formulated by the local development councils. (b) Within thirty (30) days after the receipt of copies of such ordinances and resolutions, the sangguniang panlalawigan shall examine the documents or transmit them to the provincial attomey, or if there be none, to the provincial prosecutor for prompt examination. The provincial attomey or provincial prosecutor shall, within a period of ten (I O) days from receipt of the documents, inform the sangguniang panlalawigan in writing of his comments or recommendations, which may be considered by the sangguniang panlalawigan in making its decision. (c) If the sangguniang panlalawigan finds that such an ordinance or resolution is beyond the power conferred upon the sangguniang panlungsod or sangguniang bayan concemed, it shall declare such ordinance or resolution invalid in whole or in part. The sangguniang panlalawigan shall enter its action in the minutes and shall advise the corresponding city or municipal authorities of the action it has taken. (d) If no action has been taken by the sanqqunianq panlalawiqan within thirty (30) days after submission of such an ordinance or resolution. the same shall be oresumed consistent with law and therefore vali4." (Emphasis supplied) Accordingly, as a matter of course, ordinances are already given legal effect even if the same is still pending review by the Sanggunian Panlalawigan upon the arrival of the time provided for in the effectivity clause of the ordinance. For information, Municipal roads are roads within the poblaciön, roads that connect to Provincial and National roads, and roads that provide inter-barangay connections to major municipal and city infrastructure without traversing Provincial Roads. To put emphasis, Item I (Additional Roles of Local Chief Executives) of the subject MC, specifically, first paragraph thereof mentioned that Provincial Govemors shall spearhead clearing operations in all provincial roads, and interface with the Mayors to discuss the implementation of the MC and formulation of strategies for the improved and continuous conduct of road clearing operations in the LGUs- With respect to the national roads, Item II(f) of MC No. 2020-027 mentioned that LGUs may coordinate with the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) in conducting road clearing operations in national roads or any other roads under its direct management and maintenance. Page 3 of 4

Hence, we are of the view that road clearing operations in provincial and national roads shall be coordinated with the provincial govemment and DPWH, respectively. The opinion shall be without prejudice to any contrary opinion that will be rendered by more competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: MARL GAN ry for Local Govemment OUSLG,'MLl/LLLS-LRALLD/lasrn copy furnished: ATTY. ANTHONY C.
